detailed_rationale:
Campus Activewear is India's leading sports-and-athleisure footwear brand (~17% share of the scaled S&A segment), and its FY26 numbers show a real, continuing growth story: sales of Rs 1,774 Cr (+11.4% YoY) and net profit of Rs 150 Cr (+24% YoY), with EPS up to Rs 4.91 from Rs 3.97. Return ratios remain strong (ROE 16.8%, ROCE 26.1%), debtor days have improved from 54 to 41 (working-capital discipline), and debt is moderate relative to the scale of the business (D/E ~0.26).

The reason the quant score flags a Sell on the 1-year lens is almost certainly valuation and momentum rather than any fundamental deterioration -- at a PE near 46-50x, the stock is priced for a materially higher growth rate than the low-teens the company is currently delivering, and our value_score for the name is weak (37.7/100). Promoter holding has drifted down modestly (74.0% to 72.1% over three years) while domestic institutions have added meaningfully (6.7% to 11.4%), a fairly normal ownership evolution for a maturing consumer-brand IPO rather than a governance flag.

We see no balance-sheet stress, no earnings-quality one-off, and no governance red flag in the data available -- this reads like a genuine quality-compounder story that has simply become expensive, which is a valuation call, not a fundamental one, and our mandate here is fundamental-only.
recommendation_rationale: We are rescuing the quant Sell to Hold. The 1-year quant score is being driven by a rich valuation and possibly softening price momentum, not by any fundamental deterioration -- revenue, profit, margins, returns and working capital are all moving in the right direction, and there is no balance-sheet or governance issue to point to. A pure valuation concern does not, on its own, meet the bar for a fundamental Sell in our framework.
summary: Campus Activewear, India's leading sports-and-athleisure footwear brand, continues to grow at a healthy double-digit clip (FY26 sales +11.4%, profit +24%) with strong returns on capital and improving working-capital discipline. The stock's valuation is rich relative to that growth rate, which is the main reason for caution, but we see no underlying business deterioration. We rate it a Hold.
positive_para: Campus holds the number-one position in India's scaled sports-and-athleisure footwear category (~17% share), continues to compound revenue and profit at healthy double-digit rates, and shows genuinely improving capital efficiency (ROE 16.8%, ROCE 26.1%, debtor days down from 54 to 41). There is no balance-sheet or governance red flag in the data we reviewed.
negative_para: The stock's valuation (PE ~46-50x) is demanding relative to the low-teens growth the company is currently delivering, and this valuation/growth mismatch is the most plausible explanation for the quant framework's cautious short-term score. Footwear retail also faces ongoing competitive intensity from both larger organized players and D2C entrants, which could pressure the growth rate further if unaddressed.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At roughly 46-50x earnings against low-teens actual growth, the multiple already prices in a meaningfully faster growth trajectory than the company is currently proving out -- a 'pay up for brand quality' valuation, not a bargain. This is not, however, a business showing fundamental deterioration; if growth reaccelerates toward the mid-teens the multiple becomes easier to justify, but at the current pace it leaves limited room for multiple expansion from here.
